steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

In a large skillet over medium-high heat, saute the ground turkey for 5 to 10 minutes, or until browned. Drain the turkey, stir in the tomato sauce and sugar, and set aside. In a medium bowl, combine the sour cream and cream cheese. Mix well and set aside.

Cook noodles according to package directions. Place them into a 9x13-inch baking dish, then layer the turkey mixture over the noodles. Then layer the sour cream mixture over the turkey, and top with cheese.
Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 20 to 35 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly.

raw_recipe.headline: Ground Turkey Casserole
raw_recipe.description: Its quick, fun and great! I learned this in grammar school. You may want to serve with corn bread or French bread and a salad.

review.reviewBody: Terrrrific! Easy to make, tastes great. Took the advice of previous reviewers by adding onion and garlic. I substituted with low fat cheese and sour cream and our favorite spaghetti sauce instead of tomato sauce. To avoid the dryness others mentioned, I tripled the amount of sauce to 24 oz and mixed the noodles with the meat/sauce before layering. Will make this again!

I left out the sugar to the tomato sauce and added onion and fresh mushrooms to the recipe. I sauteed the onion and mushroom first, added the turkey, then tomato sauce. I layered it in an electric skillet meat mixture first, then sour cream/cream cheese mixture, then pasta, and finally cheese. I used sharp cheddar and sprinkled with oregano.

I made some of my own mods after reading a few reviews! Added some minced garlic and a package of onion soup mix to the turkey meat, as well as a bit of cayenne and paprika. Turkey being the healthy and inexpensive choice, it can be bland - so I personally season the bleep out of mine.
I did not have a big casserole dish on hand, so I had to use my 8x9, which didn't affect it imo. Kept it saucy! Although I may add another can of tomato sauce in the future.
I also mixed a bit of onion soup mix into the sour cream/cheese mixture, and mmmmmmm!!!!
Last mod was I only had shredded Mexican blend cheese - obvs delicious, any cheese you like really!
This was cheap and easy to make, I served mine with broccoli. Will make again. :)

So of course I totally changed it based on what I had at home. Sauteed onions, garlic, cherry tomatoes cut in half and asparagus cut into small pieces. Added dried oregano, dried thyme and fresh sage as well as salt and pepper all to taste. Then browned the turkey, added in the veggie mixture and a can of organic diced tomatoes with jus. Added a little sugar and then let this simmer slowly while I cooked one pound of penne rigate. Mixed the two, put into a 9X13 glass baking pan, mixed some sour cream with cream cheese in the carton and spread it out over the pasta mixture, then put a generous helping of shredded mixed italian cheeses (did not bother using the real parmegiano reggiano or provolone since this is an American dish in my opinion) and then baked for 25 mins at 350F. I enjoy casseroles and the creativity you can have with them. My husband doesn't care for baked pasta. I'd make it again because the combinations and options are limitless - all veggie, or using beef or pork or a mixture. Easy to make and you can get creative. I never measure seasonings or much of anything, just do it by eye/taste and it comes out well.

I will give it 4 stars as is but to be fair, I made these changes and I think it is 5 star with these changes and healthier too! First,I left out the sugar (why use it, just extra calories for nothing), used 0% fat Greek yogurt in place of sour cream (I do this with everything), added sauteed garlic and onions to the turkey and a liberal sprinkle of jalapenos and reduce the cream cheese (used 1/3 fat neufchatel) to about 6 oz. it was amazing and the jalapenos give it a great boost. Also, I used rigatoni that I precooked a little firm and then heated it all in the oven till bubbly.

I made this tonight and I took advice from other viewers about the dry noodles and added a can of Rotel tomatoes to it along with the tomato sauce and half a cup of water in the mixture. I cooked in some onions and garlic and mixed it with the cooked noodles. I also blended the sour cream mix into the dish after placing it in the baking dish then added shredded cheese ( the 4 cheese) on top. came out perfect. I will certainly be making this again.

This recipe is pretty good and shows a different way of using egg noodles. However, I cut the recipe in half except for the meat and cooked chopped onion in with the ground turkey along with salt and pepper; instead of using white sugar I used 2tbs ketchup; and I would recommend lining the bottom of the baking dish with tomato sauce, then the noodles, the meat mixture, etc.

We loved it! Modified just a few things because of some reviews. I used low fat cream cheese and sour cream. I also only used about 6oz of each instead of 8. I used an entire small jar of my favorite chunky spaghetti sauce, and also spiced up my meat with garlic and minced onion. Before layering the noodles I layed them in the sauce and than layed them in the pan. They came out perfect, not dry at all :)) My kids wanted seconds!!!

So I took this recipe and sort of amped it up to a whole different level and it was absolutely amazing!! I had limited ingredients in my fridge but I had the basics of the recipe. I used Rotel diced tomatoes, black beans, corn, and a red onion (yea I know) I sautéed the black beans with the red onion some Goya, brown sugar, and garlic. In a seperate pan I heated the Rotel and mexicorn with some garlic and cayenne pepper. I then sautéed my turkey meat with some spicy taco seasoning and pepper. I combined everything into one bowl - sour cream, cream cheese, and all the fixins! I also only had macaroni noodles but hey - it worked! What a delight. Topped with cheese and baked. It was phenomenal!

Oh, this is so good! I added a diced onion and a little garlic powder to the turkey while it cooked. I let it reduce so I did not have to drain it. I think it has more flavor that way. I then added a jar of spaghetti sauce. The recipe did not specify what kind of tomato sauce. I did not add sugar. The two men in my house gobbled up a double recipe in one night! I did have about two cups myself. This would be great to take to a pot luck dinner.

Great dish I made 2 changes to the recipe first no sugar at all second I used can chilli tomatoes 14.5 oz and tomato past with 1/4cup of water in the tomato sauce I added my Italian seasoning blend which I learned from beast cook book
I added sauteed onions & mushrooms and dry ranch dressing powder for extra flavor. Also decreased the pasta.
Made exactly as described my family liked it, even had seconds.
I used a different noodle. It was good to use turkey.
everybody loved the meal very tastey
On reading the other reviews, I added half a diced onion and a load of garlic, and I salted and peppered the turkey. Other than that I followed the recipe and everyone loves it.
Easy. Yummy. Made cornbread to serve with.

This is good, but too cheesy for my daughter. She's not a fan of super cheesy foods (crazy, right?). But it is good. I even used dairy free plain yogurt in place of the sour cream and dairy free cream cheese.

This recipe has inspired my first review ever. I did some changes based on other reviews: 1. added a good TBSP of Oregano and of Basil to sauce. 2. Used 2 cans of roasted diced tomatoes + one jar of tomato basil pasta sauce. 3. Added a diced onion and 4 cloves of garlic. 5 Added a bag of frozen peas. 6. Added 2 oz. of Vodka. 7. used fresh mozzarella balls and some parmesan cheese instead of cheddar. It was SO SO SO good, my husband raved, and we calculated the Macros and they were respectable, 24% of calories from protein. Next time I'll double the ground turkey to make this an even more macro friendly dish.

Nice way to enjoy turkey for dinner. I followed this as written and luckily it came out plenty moist. Not much flavor from the turkey, but I definitely got a good mouthful of tomato and sour cream. Which I don’t mind. Sour cream is my friend. 
My tip is: follow this easy-to-do recipe closely, but perhaps tweak the turkey for more flavor. Spices, onion, garlic, seasoning, whatever your bag is. Unless of course you prefer your bird bland.
